results.title: Litespark Inference For CPUs: Ultra-Fast SIMD Framework for Ternary (1.58-bit) Language Models
results.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have transformed artificial intelligence, but their computational requirements remain prohibitive for most users. Standard inference demands expensive datacenter GPUs or cloud API access, leaving over one billion personal computers underutilized for AI workloads. Ternary models offer a path forward: their weights are constrained to {-1, 0, +1}, theoretically eliminating the need for floating-point multiplication. However, existing frameworks fail to exploit this structure, treating ternary models as dense floating-point networks. We address this gap with custom SIMD kernels that replace matrix multiplication with simple addition and subtraction operations, targeting the integer dot product instructions available on modern CPUs. Our implementation, Litespark-Inference, is pip-installable and integrates directly with Hugging-Face, achieving 18.15x higher throughput, 7.15x faster time-to-first-token and 6.03x memory reduction compared to standard PyTorch inference on Apple Silicon, with comparable or higher throughput speedups up to 95.81x on Intel and AMD processors.

results.title: UDP: Up-or-Down Precision Quantization for Large Language Models via Evolutionary Search
results.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown outstanding capabilities across complex language tasks, but come with massive computational cost and memory footprint. LLM post-training quantizers such as AWQ, SmoothQuant, and QoQ have demonstrated excellent performance under specific configurations, for example, W4A16 (four-bit weight and sixteen-bit activation) and W8A8 (eight-bit weight and eight-bit activation). However, leveraging these quantizers in a mixed-precision problem is a nontrivial task due to the colossal design space and prolonged inference time in LLMs. To address this problem, this work presents UDP (Up-or-Down Precision), a quantizer-agnostic mixed-precision framework that restricts each layer to a low/high precision pair and selects which layers to promote under deployment-driven memory/latency budgets. UDP uses KLD-guided profiling to seed high-quality candidates and a budget-aware genetic search to optimize the layer promotion set. Across Llama and Mistral models and three PTQ backends (AWQ, SmoothQuant, QoQ), UDP improves WikiText-2 perplexity by up to 0.69 over uniform low-bit baselines at the same low-precision setting and outperforms strong mixed-precision heuristics (FlattenQuant, QFeM, AsymKV) by up to 0.11 under identical budgets. In OmniServe on Llama-2-7B (1024/512 tokens), UDP preserves throughput (<inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\leq 0.5$ </tex-math></inline-formula>% vs. W4A8) while reducing p95 time-to-first-token by <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\approx 60$ </tex-math></inline-formula> ms and using <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\approx 10$ </tex-math></inline-formula>% less GPU memory than W8A8. These results show UDP produces practical mixed-precision policies aligned with real serving constraints.
